newsitem.title: FRANCE: French capital markets closing report.
newsitem.headline: French capital markets closing report.

text.p: French bond futures slipped back in a quiet session after failing to set new highs early on and settled unchanged ahead of potentially market moving events in the United States and Germany on Tuesday.
The March future broke above 130.60/62, a level it failed to breach three times last week, but ran out of steam just below the last week's contract high of 130.86.

Traders said a four billion franc France Telecom bond issue soon before the close weighed on the contract as some members of the syndicate hedged themselves by selling futures. After the bond issue the future slipped from 130.60 to 130.48.
Traders said the zone around 130.60 would be an important level for the contract to pass before retesting the highs.

Analysts said German M3 money supply data due sometime this week would be important for shaping expectations for short-term interest rate cuts, as would the German Ifo business climate survey, due on Tuesday.

A speech by Federal Reserve chairman on Tuesday at 1500 GMT was also putting traders on their guard. Although few expected him to give any clues as to what might happen at the next Fed policy council meeting on February 4, there was always a chance he could spring some surprise on the market, they said.

There was more action on the foreign exchange market where the franc fell as low as 5.50 against the dollar, the level former president Valery Giscard d'Estaing and Bank of France member Paul Marchelli both called for last autumn.

The move was driven by widespread dollar strength which also pushed the mark below 1.63. The dollar lost some ground late in the session to leave the franc at 5.4775 compared with the day's low of 5.5004.
Analysts said while the franc move would no doubt please the French authorities it remained to be seen whether the weaker level could be sustained, and the case for rate cuts remained.

"I still believe we're going to see rather weakish numbers in the coming weeks reflecting fourth-quarter sluggish growth. Therefore we will have more pressure to cut rates," Philippe Brossard, head of research at ABN Amro in Paris, said.

"A strong dollar is only one of the necessary conditions for recovery in Europe." Valerie Plagnol market economist at Credit Commercial de France, said. "There are limits to the decoupling from the U.S. and we should still cut interests in Europe. (The dollar rally) really doesn't prevent us from doing that."
The franc remained relatively stable against the mark, and was trading at 3.3728 compared with 3.3718 on Friday.

The 10-year spread between French and German benchmark yields remained unchanged at minus 16 basis points, while the steepness of the French curve, measured by the gap between two- and 10-year bonds, remained steady at 227 basis points.
March interest rate futures were also unchanged. Analysts said hopes for further interest rate cuts in the next few months continued to buoy the market.

As expected, the Bank of France left its intervention rate unchanged after today's money market tender at 3.15 percent. Its policy council next meets on January 30. Call money was also unchanged at 3-3/16 5/16 percent.
